Unlike methods that optimize color or rely on static assumptions, this approach fixes the color map (intensity ranges) and iteratively refines opacity to balance feature conspicuity, distinguishing itself from siblings like [Voxel-based Transfer Function Optimization](3259-voxel-based-transfer-function-optimization.md) by explicitly modeling occlusion via the VWS metric [S1].

The claim states that the approach fixes the color map (intensity ranges) and iteratively refines opacity to balance feature conspicuity, distinguishing itself by explicitly modeling occlusion via the VWS metric. Source [S1] confirms all these points: it explicitly states 'only the opacity of features are changed... whilst the classification of features... represented by the color map remains invariant'; it describes an 'iterative optimization approach' using the 'VWS metric' which 'takes into account... view-dependent occlusion'; and it aims to match a 'user-specified target conspicuity distribution'.
